notebooks.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
notebooks.summary: Physical causal memory is operationally valid when internal states enable predictive control over future dynamics. Recent findings demonstrate that this causal influence is bounded by thermodynamic uncertainty relations and dissipation limits.
notebooks.findings: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations impose fundamental limits on the dissipation required for maintaining a causal memory state. [peer-342d102f4cc50bf0f7e3c3bb]
notebooks.limitations: Findings are constrained by classical coarse-graining approximations and idealized assumptions regarding non-equilibrium steady states. The distinction between emergent statistical correlations and genuine causal influence remains sensitive to measurement scales.
notebooks.next_questions: How do non-Markovian dynamics in the environment influence the thermodynamic cost of causal state updates?
notebooks.reason: Notebook updated to integrate thermodynamic uncertainty bounds and statistical limitations on causal inference.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Costs and Nonequilibrium Limits of Memory Retention
notebooks.summary: Revised analysis integrating open dissipative substrate models and nonequilibrium electrode conditions for reliable memory retention.
notebooks.findings: Memory writing and retention in open dissipative substrates entail thermodynamic entropy production bounds that extend Landauer's principle by incorporating synaptic degeneracy, coarse-graining, and nonequilibrium conditions. [source-bbac57fad2784d1b]
notebooks.limitations: Models remain specific to idealized bistable units and quantum dot assumptions; broad empirical validation across diverse biological and artificial media requires further work.
notebooks.next_questions: What are the precise scaling relations between memory refresh rates and entropy production in generic non-Markovian environments?

detail.title: Operational Criteria for Physical Causal Memory
detail.summary: Physical causal memory is operationally valid when internal states enable predictive control over future dynamics. Recent findings demonstrate that this causal influence is bounded by thermodynamic uncertainty relations and dissipation limits.
detail.findings: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations impose fundamental limits on the dissipation required for maintaining a causal memory state. [peer-342d102f4cc50bf0f7e3c3bb]
detail.limitations: Findings are constrained by classical coarse-graining approximations and idealized assumptions regarding non-equilibrium steady states. The distinction between emergent statistical correlations and genuine causal influence remains sensitive to measurement scales.
detail.next_questions: How do non-Markovian dynamics in the environment influence the thermodynamic cost of causal state updates?
detail.reason: Notebook updated to integrate thermodynamic uncertainty bounds and statistical limitations on causal inference.
